about: House recipes, batch 04 (slice B): written by Claude in a Max-plan session, original, ai-draft. Nutrition is a per-serve estimate kept as data only.

recipes.title: Vanilla Birthday Sponge Squares
recipes.summary: Soft vanilla sponge squares with a thin buttercream layer, easy to cut and carry to a party.
steps: Heat the oven to 160°C fan (180°C conventional). Grease and line a 20cm square tin with baking paper.
Beat the 175g butter and the caster sugar for 4 minutes until pale and fluffy. Beat in the eggs one at a time, then the vanilla.
Fold in the flour and milk until just smooth, scrape into the tin and level the top.
Bake for 30 minutes until golden and a skewer in the centre comes out clean. Cool in the tin for 10 minutes, then lift out onto a rack to cool completely.
Beat the 80g butter with the icing sugar and 1 tbsp water until fluffy, spread over the cold cake and cut into 12 squares.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 square.
Storage: keeps 3 days in an airtight container in a cool spot; the iced cake freezes for 2 months.

recipes.title: Victoria Sponge Fingers
recipes.summary: Two light sponge layers sandwiched with jam and whipped cream, cut into tidy fingers.
steps: Heat the oven to 170°C fan (190°C conventional). Grease and line two 18cm square tins.
Beat the butter and caster sugar for 4 minutes until pale and fluffy, then beat in the eggs and vanilla one at a time.
Fold in the flour and baking powder, divide between the tins and level the tops.
Bake for 22 to 25 minutes until risen, golden and springy to a light press. Cool in the tins for 5 minutes, then turn out onto a rack.
Whip the cream with the icing sugar to soft peaks. Spread one sponge with the jam, then the cream, top with the second sponge and cut into 10 fingers.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 finger.
Storage: best the day it is filled; keep covered in the fridge for up to 2 days.

recipes.title: Lemon Chiffon Cake Wedges
recipes.summary: A tall, airy cake made with oil and whipped egg whites, finished with a light lemon glaze.
steps: Heat the oven to 160°C fan (180°C conventional). Leave a 20cm tube tin ungreased so the cake can climb the sides.
Whisk the flour, 120g of the sugar, baking powder and salt in a bowl. Make a well and add the oil, water, egg yolks and lemon zest, then whisk to a smooth batter.
Whisk the egg whites to soft peaks, then add the remaining 80g sugar a spoonful at a time until stiff and glossy.
Fold a third of the whites into the batter to loosen it, then gently fold in the rest. Pour into the tin and bake for 45 minutes until deep golden and a skewer comes out clean.
Turn the tin upside down onto a bottle neck and cool completely. Run a knife around the edges, release, then drizzle with the icing sugar mixed with the lemon juice and cut into 12 wedges.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian.
Storage: keeps 3 days covered at room temperature.

recipes.title: Orange Chiffon Slices
recipes.summary: Cloud-soft orange chiffon baked in a loaf tin, sliced thickly for the lunchbox.
steps: Heat the oven to 160°C fan (180°C conventional). Line the base of a 23cm loaf tin with baking paper and leave the sides ungreased.
Whisk the flour, 100g of the sugar, baking powder and salt. Add the oil, orange juice, zest, vanilla and egg yolks and whisk until smooth.
Whisk the egg whites to soft peaks, add the remaining 70g sugar gradually and whisk to stiff, glossy peaks.
Fold a third of the whites into the batter, then fold in the rest gently so the air stays in.
Bake for 40 minutes until golden, springy and a skewer comes out clean. Cool completely in the tin before slicing into 12.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian.
Storage: keeps 3 days in an airtight container.

recipes.title: Classic Butter Loaf Cake Slices
recipes.summary: A dense, buttery loaf with a fine crumb, perfect with a cup of tea or sliced fruit.
steps: Heat the oven to 150°C fan (170°C conventional). Grease and line a 23cm loaf tin.
Beat the butter and sugar for 5 minutes until very pale and fluffy. Add the eggs one at a time, beating well, then the vanilla.
Fold in the flour, baking powder and salt alternately with the milk until just combined.
Scrape into the tin and bake for 60 minutes until deep golden, the top has cracked and a skewer comes out clean. Cover loosely with foil if it browns too quickly.
Cool in the tin for 15 minutes, then turn out and slice into 12 even slices.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 slice.
Storage: keeps 4 days wrapped; freezes well in slices for 2 months.

recipes.title: Glazed Pineapple Ring Cake Squares
recipes.summary: A buttery brown sugar and pineapple topping baked over a soft vanilla cake, turned out and cut into squares.
steps: Heat the oven to 160°C fan (180°C conventional). Line a 20cm square tin with baking paper.
Stir the melted butter and brown sugar together, spread over the base of the tin and arrange the drained pineapple on top.
Beat the softened butter and caster sugar for 3 minutes until pale. Beat in the eggs and vanilla, then fold in the flour and pineapple juice.
Spoon the batter over the pineapple and level it. Bake for 40 minutes until golden and a skewer comes out clean.
Rest for 5 minutes, then turn out onto a board while still warm, peel off the paper and cut into 12 squares.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 square.
Storage: best within 2 days; keep covered at room temperature.

recipes.title: Apple Upside-Down Cake
recipes.summary: Caramelised cinnamon apples under a tender sponge, flipped to show the glossy top.
steps: Heat the oven to 160°C fan (180°C conventional). Line a 20cm round cake tin with baking paper.
Melt the 50g butter with the brown sugar in a frying pan, add the apples and cinnamon and cook for 5 minutes until just soft and glossy. Spread over the base of the tin.
Beat the softened butter and caster sugar for 3 minutes until pale. Beat in the eggs, then fold in the flour and milk.
Spoon over the apples and level. Bake for 40 to 45 minutes until golden and a skewer comes out clean.
Rest for 5 minutes, then turn out onto a plate and cut into 12 wedges.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 wedge.
Storage: keeps 2 days covered; reheat a wedge for 20 seconds in the microwave if wanted.

recipes.title: Pear Upside-Down Ginger Cake
recipes.summary: Spiced ginger sponge over caramelised pear slices, sticky and fragrant.
steps: Heat the oven to 160°C fan (180°C conventional). Line a 20cm round cake tin with baking paper.
Melt the 50g butter and the first 80g brown sugar in a frying pan, add the pears and cook for 4 minutes until glossy. Arrange in the tin.
Beat the softened butter, remaining 100g brown sugar and golden syrup for 3 minutes. Beat in the eggs, then fold in the flour, ginger, cinnamon and milk.
Spoon over the pears. Bake for 45 minutes until a skewer comes out clean and the top is deep golden.
Rest for 5 minutes, turn out onto a plate and cut into 12 wedges.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 wedge.
Storage: keeps 3 days covered at room temperature.

recipes.title: Chocolate Birthday Traybake
recipes.summary: A fudgy chocolate sheet cake with a glossy chocolate icing, made for sharing.
steps: Heat the oven to 160°C fan (180°C conventional). Grease and line a 20cm by 30cm tin.
Beat the butter and sugar for 4 minutes until pale. Beat in the eggs one at a time.
Sift in the flour, cocoa and baking powder, add the milk and fold until smooth. Spread into the tin.
Bake for 28 to 30 minutes until the cake springs back and a skewer comes out clean. Cool in the tin.
Heat the cream until steaming, pour over the broken chocolate, stand for 2 minutes and stir until glossy. Cool for 10 minutes, spread over the cake and cut into 12.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 piece.
Storage: keeps 4 days in an airtight container.

recipes.title: Coconut Vanilla Celebration Cake
recipes.summary: A moist coconut milk sponge topped with vanilla icing and toasted coconut, light enough for a crowd.
steps: Heat the oven to 160°C fan (180°C conventional). Grease and line a 20cm square tin.
Beat the butter and caster sugar for 4 minutes until pale. Beat in the eggs and vanilla.
Fold in the flour, the first 30g coconut and the 200ml coconut milk until smooth, then spread into the tin.
Bake for 35 minutes until golden and a skewer comes out clean. Cool completely.
Toast the last 30g coconut in a dry pan for 2 minutes until pale gold. Mix the icing sugar with 2 tbsp coconut milk, spread over the cake, scatter with the coconut and cut into 12.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 piece.
Storage: keeps 3 days in an airtight container.

recipes.title: Madeira Cake Slices
recipes.summary: A classic lemony loaf with a firm, even crumb that slices cleanly.
steps: Heat the oven to 150°C fan (170°C conventional). Grease and line a 23cm loaf tin.
Beat the butter, caster sugar and lemon zest for 4 minutes until pale and fluffy.
Beat in the eggs one at a time, then fold in the flour, lemon juice and milk.
Spoon into the tin, level, and sprinkle with the 1 tbsp sugar. Bake for 50 to 55 minutes until golden with a split top and a skewer comes out clean.
Cool in the tin for 10 minutes, turn out and slice into 12.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian.
Storage: keeps 5 days wrapped in baking paper in a tin.

recipes.title: Almond Orange Syrup Cake
recipes.summary: A moist almond cake soaked in orange syrup, naturally wheat free if gluten-free baking powder is used.
steps: Heat the oven to 160°C fan (180°C conventional). Grease and line a 20cm round cake tin.
Whisk the eggs and caster sugar for 4 minutes until thick and pale.
Fold in the almond meal, baking powder, zest and oil, pour into the tin and bake for 40 to 45 minutes until golden and a skewer comes out clean.
Simmer the orange juice and the 3 tbsp sugar for 5 minutes until slightly syrupy.
Prick the warm cake with a skewer, pour over the syrup, cool in the tin and cut into 12 wedges.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Contains nuts and eggs.
Storage: keeps 4 days covered; it improves on day two.

recipes.title: Marble Loaf Cake
recipes.summary: Vanilla and chocolate batters swirled together for a pretty striped slice.
steps: Heat the oven to 160°C fan (180°C conventional). Grease and line a 23cm loaf tin.
Beat the butter and sugar for 4 minutes until pale. Beat in the eggs, then fold in the flour, milk and vanilla.
Spoon half the batter into a second bowl. Mix the cocoa and hot water to a paste and stir into that half.
Drop alternate spoonfuls of the batters into the tin, then drag a skewer through once or twice to swirl.
Bake for 50 to 55 minutes until a skewer comes out clean. Cool in the tin for 10 minutes, turn out and slice into 12.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian.
Storage: keeps 4 days in an airtight container.

recipes.title: Carrot Cake Traybake Squares
recipes.summary: Spiced carrot cake with walnuts and a light cream cheese frosting.
steps: Heat the oven to 160°C fan (180°C conventional). Grease and line a 20cm square tin.
Whisk the eggs, sugar and oil for 2 minutes. Fold in the carrot, then the flour, baking powder, cinnamon, nutmeg and walnuts.
Spread into the tin and bake for 35 minutes until firm, golden and a skewer comes out clean. Cool completely.
Beat the cream cheese, butter and icing sugar until smooth. Spread over the cake and cut into 12 squares.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Contains nuts.
Storage: keep in the fridge for up to 4 days because of the frosting.

recipes.title: Spiced Pumpkin Loaf
recipes.summary: A tender spiced loaf made with roasted pumpkin purée, lovely with butter.
steps: Heat the oven to 160°C fan (180°C conventional). Grease and line a 23cm loaf tin.
Whisk the pumpkin, eggs, sugar and oil until smooth.
Fold in the flour, baking powder and spices, then the walnuts, until just combined.
Scrape into the tin and bake for 50 to 55 minutes until deep golden and a skewer comes out clean.
Cool in the tin for 10 minutes, turn out and slice into 12.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Contains nuts.
Storage: keeps 4 days wrapped; freezes well sliced.

recipes.title: Pineapple Coconut Layer Cake Wedges
recipes.summary: Two spiced pineapple and coconut layers with a cream cheese frosting, a hummingbird-style cake without banana.
steps: Heat the oven to 160°C fan (180°C conventional). Grease and line two 18cm round cake tins.
Whisk the eggs, caster sugar and oil for 2 minutes. Fold in the pineapple, flour, baking powder, cinnamon and coconut.
Divide between the tins and bake for 30 to 35 minutes until golden and a skewer comes out clean. Cool completely.
Beat the cream cheese, butter and icing sugar until smooth. Sandwich the layers with a third of the frosting and spread the rest on top, then cut into 12 wedges.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian.
Storage: keep in the fridge for up to 3 days; bring to room temperature to serve.

recipes.title: Honey Ginger Loaf Slices
recipes.summary: A sticky, gently spiced loaf sweetened with honey and golden syrup.
steps: Heat the oven to 150°C fan (170°C conventional). Grease and line a 23cm loaf tin.
Melt the butter, honey, golden syrup and sugar together over low heat, stirring until smooth. Cool for 5 minutes.
Whisk in the eggs and milk, then fold in the flour, ginger, baking powder and bicarbonate soda.
Pour into the tin and bake for 45 to 50 minutes until risen and a skewer comes out clean.
Cool in the tin for 15 minutes, turn out and slice into 12.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian.
Storage: keeps 5 days wrapped; the stickiness improves after a day.

recipes.title: Chocolate Beetroot Cake Squares
recipes.summary: A moist chocolate cake made with cooked beetroot, which adds sweetness and keeps it soft.
steps: Heat the oven to 160°C fan (180°C conventional). Grease and line a 20cm square tin.
Whisk the beetroot, eggs, sugar and oil until smooth.
Sift in the flour, cocoa and baking powder and fold until combined. Spread into the tin.
Bake for 30 to 35 minutes until a skewer comes out clean. Cool completely in the tin.
Heat the cream until steaming, pour over the broken chocolate, stand for 2 minutes and stir until glossy. Spread over the cake, set for 20 minutes and cut into 12.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 square.
Storage: keeps 3 days in the fridge in an airtight container.

recipes.title: Cinnamon Sour Cream Crumb Cake Squares
recipes.summary: A tender sour cream cake topped with a thick cinnamon crumble.
steps: Heat the oven to 160°C fan (180°C conventional). Grease and line a 20cm square tin.
Mix the brown sugar, 60g flour, cinnamon and melted butter into big crumbs and set aside.
Beat the softened butter and caster sugar for 3 minutes. Beat in the eggs, sour cream and vanilla, then fold in the 240g flour, baking powder and bicarbonate soda.
Spread into the tin and scatter with the crumbs. Bake for 40 minutes until golden and a skewer comes out clean.
Cool in the tin for 15 minutes, lift out and cut into 12 squares.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian.
Storage: keeps 3 days in an airtight container.

recipes.title: Orange Polenta Cake Wedges
recipes.summary: A rustic gluten-free-style cake of polenta and almond meal with orange syrup.
steps: Heat the oven to 160°C fan (180°C conventional). Grease and line a 20cm round cake tin.
Beat the butter and caster sugar for 4 minutes until pale. Beat in the eggs one at a time with a spoonful of the almond meal to stop curdling.
Fold in the rest of the almond meal, polenta, baking powder and orange zest, then spread into the tin.
Bake for 40 minutes until golden and a skewer comes out clean.
Simmer the orange juice and the 3 tbsp sugar for 4 minutes. Spoon over the warm cake, cool in the tin and cut into 12 wedges.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Contains nuts and eggs. Use gluten-free baking powder for a gluten-free cake.
Storage: keeps 4 days covered.

recipes.title: Flourless Chocolate Almond Cake Wedges
recipes.summary: A dense, fudgy flourless cake with melted chocolate and almond meal.
steps: Heat the oven to 160°C fan (180°C conventional). Grease and line a 20cm springform tin.
Melt the chocolate and butter together gently, stir and cool for 5 minutes.
Whisk the egg yolks with 60g of the sugar until pale, then stir in the chocolate mixture, almond meal and cocoa.
Whisk the egg whites to soft peaks, add the remaining 60g sugar and whisk until glossy. Fold a third into the chocolate mixture, then fold in the rest.
Bake for 28 to 30 minutes until the edges are set and the centre has a slight wobble. Cool in the tin, then cut into 12 wedges.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Contains nuts and eggs.
Storage: keeps 4 days in the fridge; serve at room temperature.

recipes.title: Sugar-Reduced Lemon Loaf
recipes.summary: A tangy lemon loaf using about half the sugar of a classic recipe, sweetened further by apple sauce.
steps: Heat the oven to 160°C fan (180°C conventional). Grease and line a 23cm loaf tin.
Whisk the eggs and sugar for 2 minutes, then whisk in the apple sauce, oil, yoghurt, zest and juice.
Fold in the flour and baking powder until just combined.
Pour into the tin and bake for 40 to 45 minutes until golden and a skewer comes out clean.
Cool in the tin for 10 minutes, turn out and slice into 12.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. About 6g sugar a slice, against 15g in a classic loaf.
Storage: keeps 3 days in an airtight container.

recipes.title: Sugar-Reduced Apple Oat Muffins
recipes.summary: Soft muffins sweetened mostly with apple and a little honey, with oats for fibre.
steps: Heat the oven to 160°C fan (180°C conventional). Line a 12-hole muffin tin with paper cases.
Whisk the eggs, honey, oil and yoghurt until smooth. Stir in the grated apple.
Fold in the flour, oats, baking powder and cinnamon until just combined.
Divide between the cases and bake for 20 to 22 minutes until golden and a skewer comes out clean.
Cool in the tin for 5 minutes, then on a rack.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 muffin. About 7g sugar each.
Storage: keeps 3 days in an airtight container; freezes for 2 months.
